title: [Mouse Without Borders] MWB leaks ~15 handles/s (Event/Key/WaitCompletionPacket on the cert stores) after an MWB restart while Settings is open; stops when PowerToys.Settings exits

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplies a repeatable restart trigger, handle-type measurements, a no-restart control, and a Settings-exit control. The proposed signer-check connection is plausible but unconfirmed, so a maintainer reproduction with handle-stack attribution is the next step.
evidence: The report identifies PowerToys 0.103.3052.0 x64, MWB service mode off, and a toggle while Settings remains open as the trigger.
The reported process grows Event, Key, and WaitCompletionPacket handles at about 14-15 per second; a no-restart control stays flat and ending Settings stops growth.
The issue identifies certificate-store handles and suggests the SettingsSync signer check, but provides no allocation stack proving that attribution.

Current source at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 verifies the peer on a recreated SettingsSync connection; the inspected managed and native certificate resources have explicit disposal paths.
The linked #51448 report is a separate service-mode SYSTEM issue with a different trigger and Token/Event/Thread profile.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the restart trigger on a current build and capture allocation/retention stacks for the growing handle types before changing signer verification or resource-lifetime code.

fix_assessment.rationale: A source-specific code change is not justified yet: the suspected verification path has explicit disposal scopes and no captured allocation stack identifies an app-owned leak. This is not a dismissal; the maintainer reproduction action remains necessary to locate the retaining owner before a fix can be selected.

issue_context.summary: Restarting Mouse Without Borders while Settings remains open is reported to cause rapid Event, Key, and WaitCompletionPacket handle growth in the user-session MWB process; ending Settings stops the growth.
known_information: The reporter gives a repeatable PowerToys 0.103.3052.0 scenario with MWB service mode off, Settings left open, and MWB toggled off/on to start a new process.
The reporter measured roughly 14-15 handles per second, primarily Event, Key, and WaitCompletionPacket handles; a control run without restarting MWB while Settings is open remained flat.
Ending the Settings process reportedly stops handle growth. The attached report is described as manually redacted; it was not downloaded or inspected.

Current upstream main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 verifies the peer process when a SettingsSync pipe is newly connected; the check reaches NamedPipePeerVerification.TryVerifyPeerProcess and its signing-policy path.

The inspected signing-policy path scopes X509Store, X509Chain, embedded stores, and certificate collections for disposal, and wraps native certificate-store/message handles in SafeHandle types; this does not establish that the suspected path is leak-free at runtime.
The maintainer comment on #51448 explicitly distinguishes this user-session Event/Key/WaitCompletionPacket profile from that issue's service-mode SYSTEM Token/Event/Thread profile.
inferences: The restart-while-Settings-is-open trigger and reported certificate-store handles are consistent with repeated SettingsSync peer verification, but no allocation stack proves that this call path owns the retained handles.
The source's explicit disposal paths make a missing application-level dispose non-obvious; runtime/provider behavior or another repeated path remains possible.
The reported input failures may correlate with the resource growth, but the issue says that relationship is still being tested.
issue_context.analysis: The report is detailed enough for a maintainer reproduction, but the suspected signer-check path is not proven. Current source explicitly disposes the managed certificate/store objects and wraps native certificate handles, so do not weaken signer verification, cache results, or propose a cleanup patch until a current-build handle trace identifies the allocating stack.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body and all comments; the report supplies a repeated restart trigger, a no-restart control, handle-type measurements, and a Settings-exit control.
Inspected current upstream main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368: MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.GetSettingsSyncHelperAsync verifies the peer when recreating the SettingsSync stream.

Traced TryVerifyServer through TryVerifyPeerProcess and the signing-policy path; the inspected X509Store, X509Chain, embedded-store, certificate-collection, and native SafeHandle paths have explicit disposal.
Confirmed PR #50480 is merged; its existence does not prove that the reported leak is caused by signer verification or that the current resource lifetime is correct.
Did not download or inspect the attached diagnostic archive; the issue body contains sufficient redacted reproduction details for the next maintainer step.

actions.label: Trace MWB handles after a SettingsSync restart

reproduce.version_requirement: Reported PowerToys 0.103.3052.0 x64 with service mode off; repeat on current main or a current candidate build.
prerequisites: Use two controlled Windows test machines paired through Mouse Without Borders.
Keep PowerToys Settings running while monitoring the user-session Mouse Without Borders process; do not use or publish real credential values.
steps: Record the MWB process PID and baseline counts for Event, Key, and WaitCompletionPacket handles.
With Settings open, toggle Mouse Without Borders off and back on to start a new MWB process.
Sample the new process's handle counts at short intervals and capture allocation/retention stacks for the growing object types.
End the Settings process and observe whether growth stops; repeat a control run with Settings open but without restarting MWB.
Repeat on current source while recording SettingsSync peer-verification invocation counts; compare those counts with handle growth without weakening or bypassing signature checks.
reproduce.expected_result: Either the reported growth reproduces and a specific allocation/retention stack is identified, or current-build measurements show no growth; the Settings-open/no-restart control remains distinguishable from the restart trigger.

status.label: Maintainer reproduction needed
status.detail: The reported leak has a controlled trigger, but its allocation owner is unconfirmed.

next_action.label: Capture handle allocation stacks
next_action.reason: Attribute the growing handles before selecting a code-level fix.
